speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've been experiencing worsening vision and a headache for three weeks; to start our workup, can you describe the exact nature of the vision changes, such as blurriness, loss of peripheral vision, or floaters?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age and the progressive nature of the vision loss with headache, have you noticed any new visual disturbances like double vision, a "curtain" over your vision, or pain specifically when moving your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

Given your age, the combination of a new headache and progressive vision loss is highly concerning for this condition. I am immediately requesting an urgent ESR and CRP blood test and requesting images of your temporal arteries to confirm the diagnosis and prevent permanent blindness.
